newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia's Kaunda urges West to maintain aid cuts.
newsitem.headline: Zambia's Kaunda urges West to maintain aid cuts.

text.p: Zambia's former president Kenneth Kaunda, prevented by the government from taking part in elections last year, urged the West on Tuesday to keep up pressure on Zambia to force democratic reform.
Economic pressure and withheld aid was the only way to press President Frederick Chilbua's government for peaceful change, he said.

"Your aid cuts have presented us with an opportunity to effect change without violence. You have helped us and please, I pray that you help us until we change," Kaunda said in comments addressed to the West at a news conference.

Western governments led by the United States cut aid to Zambia last year in protest at Chiluba's decision to push through legislation that effectively banned some candidates, including Kaunda, from challenging him in elections.
Chiluba's Movement for Multiparty Democracy (MMD) won the poll which was boycotted by seven opposition parties including Kaunda's United National Independence Party.

The former president, who led Zambia to independence from Britain in 1964 and then governed for 27 years, said on Tuesday his party did not recognise Chiluba's government and would fight it peacefully.
"A little later we may fight a little harder," he said.
Chiluba took power from Kaunda in the country's first multi-party polls in 1991.
Zambia's opposition is demanding fresh polls, after last November's election process was found by observers to be flawed.
Foreign aid accounts for around a third of Zambia's 1,489.1 billion kwacha ($1.1 billion) national budget.
